verdict.rationale: Portkey documents its own controls for limiting API keys: per-key budget and rate limits that stop usage once reached, plus model allow-lists at org and workspace level. Provider credentials are kept out of code behind Portkey keys. This bounds what an agent's credential can spend and do, but the evidence never shows permission scopes on an individual key or agent-specific credential issuance. Missing for 10: documented per-key permission or endpoint scopes, per-key model restrictions (allow-lists are only shown at org/workspace level), an agent-specific key issuance workflow, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Configure budget and rate limits on API keys to effectively manage AI spending and usage across your organization
Budget limits allow you to set maximum LLM spending or token usage thresholds on your API keys, automatically preventing further usage when limits are reached.
Fine-grained control: budgets, rate limits, and model allow-lists at both org and workspace level.
Provider credentials stored securely, never exposed in code
